Read-only review of `a330fbb` against `6bc9d94` and `/tmp/b2-design.md`. Findings are from source inspection. No files were changed, and no builds or tests were run.

1. **P0 · SIGTERM can still hang during terminal teardown.** Stop reading the client’s macOS PTY, let the daemon disconnect while the client is between writes, then send SIGTERM while `guard.leave()` is blocked in `tcdrain()`. The second signal branch restores raw mode and returns without running the output-discard path. Darwin can then wait for the same unread output when the controlling session leader exits. Fix by running bounded output cleanup from both signal branches and testing a signal delivered after normal teardown starts. [attach.rs:174](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/attach.rs:174) · [terminal.rs:119](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/terminal.rs:119) · [Darwin process exit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/main/bsd/kern/kern_exit.c#L2093)

2. **P1 · The key fallthrough still loses a key if the renderer clears copy mode first.** Resize a pane with an active selection and type `x`. If input clones `Some(copy_mode)`, then render clears it before input reacquires the session lock, the `is_some_and` callback never runs. `mapped` stays `true` and `x` never reaches the PTY. Fix by marking the key consumed only after resolving a mode under the lock. The existing resize test covers invalidation by the input handler itself. [attach.rs:1380](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:1380) · [attach.rs:2425](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:2425)

3. **P1 · A stamped entry can copy from a different terminal screen.** Display `PRIMARY`, switch to a same-sized alternate screen containing `ALTERNATE`, then deliver EnterCopyMode stamped with the primary frame and press `y`. `Drawn` records the old history coordinates, but `CopyView::new` takes the screen identity from the current VT and accepts the old coordinates. OSC 52 can copy `A` even though the stamped frame showed `P`. Fix by stamping the presented screen generation and rejecting an entry whose generation no longer maps. [copy_mode.rs:55](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:55) · [copy_mode.rs:72](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:72)

4. **P1 · A stamped drag can yank from a newer copy page.** In copy mode, press PageDown and drag horizontally before the new frame is written. The drag still carries the old page’s stamp. The handler accepts it because the entry viewport is unchanged, then clamps both old source endpoints into the current page through `set_cursor`. The release can yank the same columns from a different row. Fix by preserving the stamped source coordinates through extraction, or cancelling the gesture when those coordinates cannot be represented in the current view. [attach.rs:3083](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:3083) · [copy_mode.rs:287](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:287)

5. **P1 · Search can still land and yank under the hint bar.** In a five-row pane backed by a five-row grid, put the only `TOKEN` on the last row and run `/TOKEN`, Enter, `y`. `max_top` reserves five source rows while only four are readable. `reveal` cannot scroll far enough and assigns the hit directly to the cursor. The cursor paints its glyph over the hint and OSC 52 copies `T`. Fix by bounding navigation with the readable height and rendering the remaining source rows safely at the bottom. [copy_mode.rs:127](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:127) · [copy_mode.rs:594](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:594)

6. **P1 · Reusing a host image ID can reverse which picture is on top.** Place opaque red A, then opaque blue B over it. In one redraw, delete A’s placement while retaining its bitmap and put A back at the same cell with a new placement ID. Raster draws A last. Kitty keeps B on top because B retains the larger host ID and the fallback gives the new A placement its old ID. Fix by carrying placement order in the emitted z-index and updating it when order changes. [kitty_emit.rs:179](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs:179) · [shux-raster/lib.rs:490](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-raster/src/lib.rs:490) · [Kitty stacking rules](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/#controlling-displayed-image-layout)

7. **P1 · A visible crop disappears when the client supplies no cell pixels.** Fit a `5×5` source into a `2×1` cell box, then pan one cell right. At the declared `9×19` metrics the image is 18 pixels wide. Neither retained whole source pixel starts on a cell boundary, so `place` returns `None` and Kitty drops the picture while raster draws it. This affects older clients and current clients whose terminal reports no pixel dimensions. Fix with a cell-aligned fallback that retains the visible crop when the subcell offset is unavailable. [kitty_emit.rs:313](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs:313)

8. **P2 · The wheel regression test never exercises a stamped wheel event.** The test publishes one frame and calls `handle_wheel` with `None`. An implementation that always uses the newest sent frame passes. Fix by publishing two frames with different source rows, sending `Some(first_frame)`, and asserting the literal OSC 52 text from the first frame. [attach.rs:9861](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:9861)

FIX

### Findings

1. **P0 — SIGTERM during `guard.leave()` still hangs on macOS when the terminal stopped reading (and `/dev/tty` open failure skips cleanup)**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux-ui/src/attach.rs:174-183](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/attach.rs#L174-L183), [crates/shux-ui/src/terminal.rs:173-181](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/terminal.rs#L173-L181)
   - **Failing sequence:** On macOS, the client's terminal stops reading with unread bytes in the PTY queue; then the session ends or the daemon drops the stalled client after `WRITE_STALL`, so `run_loop` returns `Ok(ExitReason::ConnectionLost)` / `Ok(ExitReason::SessionEnded)`. `run_attach` enters `spawn_blocking(|| guard.leave())`, which blocks in `write`/`tcdrain`. The user then sends `SIGTERM`. Separately, if stdout is a PTY without a controlling terminal (`ENXIO` on `/dev/tty`), `discard_unread_output` returns immediately.
   - **Why it fails:** The `signo = signals.recv()` branch at `attach.rs:179-182` only calls `disable_raw_mode()` and returns `Ok(ExitReason::Signal(signo))` without calling `discard_unread_output(SIGNAL_RESTORE_BUDGET)`. When the caller re-raises `SIGTERM`, the process still hangs in the macOS kernel waiting for unread TTY output to drain. In `terminal.rs:176-181`, failing to open `/dev/tty` skips both `dup2` and `tcflush`.
   - **Fix:** Call `terminal::discard_unread_output(SIGNAL_RESTORE_BUDGET)` in the `signals.recv()` arm at `attach.rs:179-182`. In `discard_unread_output`, fall back to `dup(STDOUT_FILENO)` when `/dev/tty` cannot be opened.

2. **P1 — `extract_selection` truncates yanks to the current horizontal viewport after a search pan, and its test never checks the yank**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:683-691](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L683-L691), [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:724-727](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L724-L727), [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:1427-1441](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L1427-L1441)
   - **Failing sequence:** In a 3×60 pane shown in a 20×3 rect containing `"abc"` at col 0 and `"zz"` at col 49 (the exact setup of `a_pan_keeps_the_selection_it_started_with`), press `v` at `(0, 0)`, search `/zz\r` (panning `view.col` to `31`, cursor to `(49, 0)`), and press `y`.
   - **Why it fails:** `extract_selection` routes every line through `modal_span`, which clamps columns to `v.col ..= v.col + v.cols() - 1` (`31..=50`). It yanks `"                  z"` (cols 31..=49), discarding `"abc"` and cols 0..30 (and similarly drops cols 20..=49 when panning left from col 49 to col 0). `a_pan_keeps_the_selection_it_started_with` claims *"the yank still starts where `v` was pressed"* but only asserts `s.anchor == anchor` and never calls `extract_selection(&vt, &s)`.
   - **Fix:** Keep `modal_span` for visible highlighting in `render_copy_overlay_inner`, but have `extract_selection` read full source coordinates across `anchor..=cursor` (preserving slice-edge clamping only when the selection stays within one unpanned slice, or spanning full rows between `start` and `end` when a pan moved an endpoint outside `v.col..v.col + v.cols()`). Assert the yanked string in `a_pan_keeps_the_selection_it_started_with`.

3. **P1 — `Drawn` omits `alt_screen`, so a primary↔alternate screen switch before stamped copy entry opens an out-of-bounds view**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:55-87](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L55-L87)
   - **Failing sequence:** A 24×80 pane on the primary screen has 500 lines of scrollback; frame `F1` is drawn with `Drawn { history: 500, evicted: 0 }`. Before `EnterCopyMode { frame: Some(F1) }` arrives, an app (`vim`, `less`, `btop`) enters the alternate screen (`\x1b[?1049h`) at the same 24×80 dimensions (`presented_total_lines() == 24`, `presented_evicted() == 0`).
   - **Why it fails:** `CopyView::new` checks only `(grid.rows(), grid.cols()) == (entry.grid_rows, entry.grid_cols)` and sets `alt_screen: vt.is_alternate_screen()` (`true`), returning `Some(CopyView { top: 500, entry_top: 500, alt_screen: true, .. })` on a 24-row screen. `CopyView::maps` then returns `true` for this broken view; `frame_view` emits `row_offset = 500, over = false`, so `compose_pane` computes `shown_rows = 24usize.saturating_sub(500) = 0`, painting the entire pane blank surplus, yanking `""`, and requiring 20+ `PgUp` presses to reach row 23. In the reverse direction (alt → primary), `EnterCopyMode` opens at scrollback line `0`.
   - **Fix:** Add `pub alt_screen: bool` to `Drawn` (from `vt.is_alternate_screen()`), and in `CopyView::new` return `None` if `vt.is_alternate_screen() != drawn.alt_screen` or if the rebased `view.top > view.max_top(vt)` so `copy_mode_over` falls back to live geometry.

4. **P1 — Search `reveal()` puts the cursor and selection on the row under the hint bar**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:519-563](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L519-L563), [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:594-611](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L594-L611)
   - **Failing sequence:** In a 5×20 pane (`rect.height == 5`, `rows() == 5`, `readable() == 4`), write `"SECRET"` on the bottom row (line `presented_total_lines() - 1`, which sits behind the hint bar). Enter copy mode and type `/SECRET\r`, then press `y`.
   - **Why it fails:** `find_and_focus` searches all `0..total` rows including `total - 1`. `reveal()` clamps `state.view.top` to `max_top(vt) = total - 5` (leaving `total - 1` at local row 4, under the hint bar), then sets `state.cursor = (hit.start, hit.line)` without enforcing `readable()`. `v.local` checks `y < v.rows()` (`4 < 5`), so the cursor renders over the hint bar, `y`/`v` yanks text from the hidden row, and pressing `l` jumps the cursor up to row 3 via `keep_cursor_in_view()`.
   - **Fix:** Limit `find_and_focus` to reachable lines (`0 ..= v.max_top(vt) + v.readable() - 1`) — or adjust `max_top` if the bottom row is meant to scroll above the hint bar — and ensure `reveal()` keeps `state.cursor` within `v.top .. v.top + v.readable()`.

5. **P1 — Eviction of `cursor.1` on an upward selection is not detected by `CopyModeState::rebase`**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:255-267](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L255-L267)
   - **Failing sequence:** With `max_scrollback = 10` and lines `e00..e15`, enter copy mode, press `v` on line 10 (`anchor = Some((0, 10))`), move/scroll up to line 2 (`cursor = (0, 2)`), then emit 5 new lines so `e00..e04` are evicted (`gone = 5`). Press `y`.
   - **Why it fails:** `rebase` uses `saturating_sub(gone)` on `self.cursor.1` (silently clamping evicted line 2 onto surviving line 0 = `e05`) and checks `checked_sub(gone)` only on `self.anchor` (`10 - 5 = Some(5)`). `self.selection_evicted` stays `false`, the selection is not cancelled, and `y` silently copies `e05..=e10` instead of rejecting the evicted selection.
   - **Fix:** Check `let cursor_evicted = self.cursor.1 < gone;` before subtracting, and when `self.anchor` is `Some((_, line))`, clear `self.anchor = None` and set `self.selection_evicted = true` if `cursor_evicted || line < gone`.

6. **P1 — Race between `run_render_loop` and `run_attach_loop` swallows a key after copy mode becomes unmappable**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux/src/attach.rs:1380-1431](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L1380-L1431) (and [crates/shux/src/attach.rs:1352-1354](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L1352-L1354))
   - **Failing sequence:** Copy mode is active with a selection on pane A; focus moves to pane B (or pane A resizes). While `run_render_loop` holds `io_state` and resolves copy mode to `None` (`modal_replaced = Some((seen, None))`), a key `x` arrives. The input task reads `attached_now` (`copy_mode == Some(seen)`) at line 1380 and waits on `pane_rect_for` / `io_state.lock()` at lines 1382–1384. `run_render_loop` releases `io_state` (line 2419) and sets `s.copy_mode = None` (line 2429) before line 1385 acquires `render_session`.
   - **Why it fails:** Line 1387 initializes `mapped = true`. Because `s.copy_mode` is now `None`, the `is_some_and` closure never runs, `mapped` stays `true`, and `if mapped { continue; }` at line 1428 drops `x` instead of forwarding it to the pane. Similarly, a `Paste` frame arriving before the render loop clears an unmappable `copy_mode` is swallowed at line 1352 without calling `resolve_copy_mode`.
   - **Fix:** Initialize `mapped = false` at line 1387 and set `mapped = true` inside the `is_some_and` closure only after `resolve_copy_mode` returns `Some(vt)`. Resolve `copy_mode` before swallowing pastes at line 1352 as well.

7. **P1 — `handle_copy_mode_mouse` clamps stale-frame drags onto the newer view (wrong yank) and swallows clicks/wheels that find copy mode ended**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux/src/attach.rs:3038-3134](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L3038-L3134)
   - **Failing sequence:**
     1. In copy mode on frame `F1` (`top = 10, col = 0`), scroll up (`cm.view.top = 0`) and before the client applies `F2`, drag-select on `F1` (`frame = Some(F1)`).
     2. In copy mode with a selection, resize the pane or move focus away, then click or scroll the wheel before the render loop clears `s.copy_mode`.
   - **Why it fails:**
     1. Line 3083 checks only `v.entry == cm.view.entry`, not `(v.top, v.col) == (cm.view.top, cm.view.col)` after rebasing. `view.source(...)` computes a row/col on `F1` (`top = 10`), then `cm.set_cursor(...)` silently clamps it into `cm.view` (`top = 0..readable`), selecting and yanking cells from `F2` instead of `F1`.
     2. When `resolve_copy_mode` returns `None` at lines 3047 or 3079, `s.copy_mode` is cleared to `None`, but `handle_copy_mode_mouse` still returns `Ok(true)` at line 3134, causing `run_attach_loop` (line 1739) to swallow the wheel/click instead of routing it.
   - **Fix:** After `let view = view.rebased(vt);`, verify `(view.top, view.col) == (cm.view.top, cm.view.col)` (else ignore the stale drag event). When `resolve_copy_mode` returns `None`, return `Ok(false)` (or prune stale `copy_mode` before `handle_app_mouse` so clicks also reach mouse-tracking apps and normal selection).

8. **P1 — `read()` drops blank lines shorter than `v.col` during multi-line yank, and `render_copy_view_into` bleeds SGR attributes onto trailing `None` cells**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:738-754](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L738-L754), [crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:802-812](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L802-L812)
   - **Failing sequence:** On a 30-column grid with 80-column history rows, pan copy mode right to `v.col = 40` via search. Line 0 (len 80) has `"AAA"` at col 40; line 1 (len 30) is shorter than `v.col`; line 2 (len 80) has `"BBB"` at col 40. Select `(40, 0)` to `(42, 2)` and press `y`. For the SGR bleed, pan so a shorter row ends at `x = 4` on a cell with a colored background (`\x1b[41m`).
   - **Why it fails:** In `read()`, `cell(0, 1)` returns `None` because `row.get(40)` is `None`, so `if cell(0, line).is_none() { continue; }` skips appending `'\n'`, yanking `"AAA\nBBB"` instead of `"AAA\n\nBBB"` even though line 1 is highlighted as selected. In `render_copy_view_into`, `write_cell` sets SGR without resetting afterward, so `None => write!(buf, " ")` paints the prior cell's background/attributes across the remaining columns of the row.
   - **Fix:** In `read()`, only skip lines missing from `vt.presented_row(line)` (not existing rows shorter than `v.col`), so existing short rows still emit `'\n'` when `line != end`. In `render_copy_view_into`, write `"\x1b[0m "` in the `None` arm.

9. **P2 — Status bar keeps `[COPY]` active on the frame that exits copy mode**
   - **Location:** [crates/shux/src/attach.rs:2221](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L2221)
   - **Failing sequence:** Focus leaves the copy-mode pane (or a resize ends a copy mode with a selection) while the session is otherwise idle; `run_render_loop` runs `resolve_copy_mode` → `None`, clears `copy_overlay`/`modal`, and schedules `modal_replaced = Some((seen, None))`.
   - **Why it fails:** Line 2221 passes `copy_mode_active: attached.copy_mode.is_some()` (`true`) instead of `modal.is_some()` (`false`), so the status bar renders `[COPY]` on the exit frame and leaves it until the next tick or event.
   - **Fix:** Pass `copy_mode_active: modal.is_some()` at line 2221.

10. **P2 — Older clients (and terminals without `TIOCGWINSZ` pixels) lose or severely truncate modestly upscaled pictures on vertical scroll**
    - **Location:** [crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs:318-322](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs#L318-L322)
    - **Failing sequence:** An older attach client (never sends `CellPixels`, so `cell_px == None`) views a `50×50` picture fitted to `c=10` (`dest = 90×90`) scrolled up by 2 rows (`vy0 = 38`), or a `100×100` picture at `c=20` (`dest = 180×180`) scrolled up by 2 rows.
    - **Why it fails:** `visible_span` finds `lead = 1` declared pixel (`1/19` of a cell), so `place(..., None)` searches `(first..end).find(|&j| lead(j) % whole == 0)`. For `50×50` at `c=10`, no `j` in `22..50` satisfies `(90*j - 1900) % 950 == 0`, so `place` returns `None` and deletes the entire 8-row picture; for `100×100` at `c=20`, the first match is `j = 95`, blanking 7 of the 8 visible rows. Base `6bc9d94` rendered both pictures.
    - **Fix:** When `real` is `None` and the cut-pixel `lead` is small (or when no later pixel aligns on a cell edge), fall back to `first` with `X=0`/`Y=0` (or only skip to a cell-aligned pixel when `lead` is a substantial fraction of a cell) rather than deleting an entire vertically-scrolled image for older clients.

FIX

reviews.content:
Ārya, I checked all ten AGY findings against `a330fbb` and compared the shutdown and image paths with `6bc9d94`. **The strongest findings are #2, #3, #5, #6, #7, and #10.** I’d also accept #4 and #9 with corrections, require a targeted macOS reproduction for #1, and hold #8 until AGY shows how normal execution produces the proposed row layout. This was a source review with a check of the image arithmetic. I didn’t run the attach scenarios or change the checkout.

AGY is strongest when it follows data across boundaries. It catches a test that checks the anchor but never checks the clipboard, identifies the exact race that drops a key, and supplies image dimensions that distinguish complete disappearance from severe cropping. Its main weakness is treating a plausible code path as proof that the stated user sequence reaches it.

| # | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **1. Shutdown hang** | **Real cleanup gap. P0 and the stated trigger need evidence.** The second signal arm skips output discard, and `/dev/tty` open failure skips both flushing and descriptor replacement. But `run_loop` awaits each render’s stdout write and flush before reading another server frame. Once it is blocked there, daemon disconnect alone cannot move it into `guard.leave()`. Target the second signal arm by establishing that the client has entered restoration before sending `SIGTERM`. Keep a bounded chance for normal restoration before discarding output, and flush the PTY that stdout actually writes to. The second arm already existed on the base. [Client loop](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/attach.rs:308) · [Cleanup](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/terminal.rs:173) |
| **2. Yank after horizontal pan** | **Confirmed. Good test catch.** The fixture keeps an anchor at column 0, but extraction starts at 31 and drops `abc`. Assert clipboard bytes in both pan directions. For multiline yanks, AGY’s proposed change still needs a clear rule for intermediate rows and wide glyphs cut by a viewport edge. [Extraction](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:680) · [Test](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:1427) |
| **3. Stamped entry after screen switch** | **Confirmed in both directions.** `Drawn` stores history coordinates without the identity of the presented screen. `CopyView::new` then pairs those old coordinates with the current screen flag, so `maps()` accepts the mismatched view. Checking the screen flag on entry lets the existing live-geometry fallback run. A bounds check alone would miss the reverse case, where row 0 is valid but points into the wrong buffer. [Copy view](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:55) · [Fallback](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:2954) |
| **4. Search under the hint bar** | **Confirmed cursor bug. The yank example overstates it.** `/SECRET` can put the cursor on the covered row and render the `S` over the hint. With no anchor, `y` copies only `S`, and `v` starts a selection. AGY’s search filter would make the final row unsearchable in a full-height view. The expected behavior should determine whether to expose that row or exclude it consistently. [Search positioning](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:594) · [Yank semantics](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:680) |
| **5. Evicted cursor endpoint** | **Confirmed wrong yank.** Saturating subtraction silently substitutes the oldest surviving row when the cursor is evicted and the anchor survives. The existing test exercises anchor eviction. Add the reverse-direction case and assert `SelectionEvicted`, with no clipboard write. [Rebase](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:255) · [Existing test](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:1689) |
| **6. Lost key and paste** | **Confirmed.** The key race is precise, and initializing `mapped` to false fixes the empty-state case. Paste has a separate early exit. Its fix needs to preserve routing for the whole paste, since `more` can split one paste across multiple frames and copy mode can change between pieces. [Input routing](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:1352) · [Render-side clear](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:2425) |
| **7. Stale mouse frame and lost event** | **Both mechanisms are real.** Mapping through `F1` and then clamping into the newer view can select different cells. Rejecting a stale drag also needs to handle a stale release so gesture state clears correctly. Returning `false` can restore downstream wheel or layout handling. App mouse and ordinary selection run earlier, so a click needs stale-mode resolution before those handlers to reach its normal destination. [Mouse dispatch](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:1617) · [Copy-mode handler](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:3045) |
| **8. Blank rows and SGR bleed** | **The local behavior is as described if the fixture exists. Reachability is missing for both claims.** Normal column resize reflows primary history to the new width and resizes all stored rows on the canvas path. A blank 30-column row still contains 30 cells. AGY needs to show how a 30-column presented grid acquires the proposed `80/30/80` row lengths, or give another reachable path to a missing cell. [Row storage](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:340) · [Resize](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:1526) · [Copy rendering](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:793) |
| **9. Stale status indicator** | **Confirmed cosmetic defect.** The indicator is `Y` on this checkout. ### Overall Verdict

Codex’s review is **unusually high signal**: **all 8 findings identify real, source-verified bugs or test gaps** in `a330fbb` with **zero false positives**, and its overall `FIX` verdict is right.

Its main weaknesses are **not** in bug detection, but in **incomplete fix prescriptions** (especially #3, #4, #6), **one misattributed scope** (#6), **understated blast radius** (#3, #7), and **minor citation/precision slips** (#1, #8).

---

### Strengths

1. **100% real defect rate across varied subsystems.** Every finding maps cleanly to actual code in `a330fbb`—spanning macOS TTY teardown, async lock races, VT screen identity, modal pointer hit-testing, hint-bar bounds, Kitty z-order/alignment math, and test coverage.
2. **Concrete minimal repros.** Almost every item gives an exact trigger sequence and observable failure rather than vague hand-waving:
   - **#2 ([attach.rs:1380-1431](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L1380-L1431), [attach.rs:2425-2431](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L2425-L2431))**: `mapped` is initialized to `true` at line 1387; if the render loop clears `s.copy_mode` between line 1380 and line 1385, `s.copy_mode.as_mut().is_some_and(...)` never runs and `if mapped { continue; }` swallows `x`. Confirmed that [the_key_after_a_resize_ends_copy_mode_reaches_the_pane](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L13498-L13521) does not trigger the render-clears-first race.
   - **#4 ([attach.rs:3083-3104](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L3083-L3104), [copy_mode.rs:286-298](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L286-L298))**: Filtering only on `v.entry == cm.view.entry` accepts a drag stamped with a pre-PageDown `CopyView`, then `cm.set_cursor(...)` clamps both endpoints into the *current* page via `keep_cursor_in_view()`, yanking columns from the wrong row.
   - **#5 ([copy_mode.rs:127-140](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L127-L140), [copy_mode.rs:594-611](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L594-L611))**: `max_top` subtracts `self.rows()` (5) instead of `self.readable()` (4), so `reveal` leaves `top = 0` and writes `state.cursor = (0, 4)` directly, bypassing `keep_cursor_in_view()`. The cursor then paints `'T'` over the hint bar at [copy_mode.rs:967-978](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L967-L978) and `y` yanks `"T"`—directly contradicting commit `9567497`’s stated invariant.
   - **#7 ([kitty_emit.rs:299-324](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs#L299-L324))**: Exact math checks out (`drawn_px(9, 19)` → `18×18`, `visible_span(5, 18, 9, 18)` → `first=3, end=5`, `whole=45`, `lead(3)=9`, `lead(4)=27`, neither `% 45 == 0` → `place()` returns `None` while `shux-raster` draws pixels `3..5`).

3. **Smart root-cause abstraction in #3.** Asking for a *screen generation* (rather than a boolean `alt_screen`) preempts primary → alt → primary ABA aliasing, which `CopyView::maps` at [copy_mode.rs:108](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L108) currently suffers from.

---

### Weaknesses, Errors, and Omissions

#### 1. Finding #3 — Proposed fix is incomplete and will not stop the reported bug
- **What codex missed:** Codex only cites [copy_mode.rs:55](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L55) and [copy_mode.rs:72](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L72) and says *"Fix by stamping the presented screen generation and rejecting an entry whose generation no longer maps."*
- **Why that fails on its own:** In [copy_mode_over](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L2954-L2968), when `CopyModeState::enter(...)` returns `None`, there is an `.or_else(...)` fallback that opens copy mode on the **current live VT** (added intentionally for resizes and asserted by [copy_mode_refuses_an_expired_stamp_and_follows_a_resize](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L13357-L13391)). If you only reject inside `CopyView::new`, `EnterCopyMode` (and `handle_wheel` at [attach.rs:4088](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L4088)) will still silently fall back to `ALTERNATE` and `y` will still copy `A`. Fixing the symptom codex describes requires changing `copy_mode_over` / `EnterCopyMode` to distinguish screen-switch rejection from the resize fallback.
- **Understated impact:** Codex only notes the 0-history case (`P` vs `A`). If the primary screen had scrollback (`drawn.history > 0`), `CopyView::new` computes `top = drawn.history + entry.row_offset` against the alternate screen (which has 0 history), placing `top` on an unrelated row or completely out of bounds of `vt.presented_row(line)`.

#### 2. Finding #6 — Misattributed narrow trigger, missing protocol context, and under-specified fix
- **Error in scope/attribution:** Codex blames the second-pass fallback at [kitty_emit.rs:179](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs#L179) and constructs a repro using a *new placement ID*. In fact, the **first-pass key match** at [kitty_emit.rs:175](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs#L175) has the exact same bug if A is deleted (`d=i`) and re-placed with the *same* `placement_id`: [grid.rs:789-818](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L789-L818) appends A to the end of `self.placements`, while `KittyEmitter` matches `l.key == k.key` and keeps A’s older, smaller `host_id`.
- **Omitted protocol nuance:** Under the Kitty graphics protocol’s stacking rules (which codex links), two placements with equal `z` stack by `(image_id, placement_id)`, so raw Kitty itself would keep `i=2` (B) over `i=1` (A) even after `i=1` is re-placed. The mismatch exists because `shux-raster` ([shux-raster/src/lib.rs:490](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-raster/src/lib.rs#L490)) paints in `self.placements` order rather than Kitty ID order. Encoding `placements` order in `z` is the right way to achieve Kitty↔raster parity, but codex frames it as if Kitty were violating its own spec rather than shux’s `placements`-order model.
- **Missing constraints in the fix:** Codex recommends encoding placement order in `z` without flagging two Kitty requirements:
  1. `z` must stay strictly `< 0` (to remain beneath copy-mode/help/toast overlays per [kitty_emit.rs:330-334](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs#L330-L334)) **and** `>= -1_073_741_824` (`-2^30`), below which Kitty renders images *under* cell backgrounds.
  2. Assigning `z` relative to `want.len()` (e.g., `-(len - idx)`) would shift `z` and force redundant `a=p` updates for every surviving image whenever a later image is added/removed; a fixed negative base + index or order-only bump avoids churn.

#### 3. Finding #4 — First proposed fix alternative is incomplete
- Codex offers two fixes: *"preserving the stamped source coordinates through extraction, or cancelling the gesture when those coordinates cannot be represented in the current view."*
- The **first alternative is broken for horizontal pans** (e.g., after `/search` pans horizontally before the stamped drag arrives): [extract_selection](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L683-L691) calls `modal_span(&state.view, ends, line)`, which clips columns to `state.view.col..state.view.col + cols`. Merely avoiding `set_cursor`’s clamp without also extracting through the stamped `CopyView` still drops or truncates the dragged columns. Either extract against the stamped `CopyView` directly or reject/cancel the gesture when `view != cm.view`.

#### 4. Finding #1 — Minor citation error and imprecise fix phrasing
- **Line citation:** Cites [terminal.rs:119](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/terminal.rs#L119) (a comment) instead of line 120 (`tcdrain`), and omits [terminal.rs:173](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/terminal.rs#L173) (`discard_unread_output`) and [dispatch.rs:126-128](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/dispatch.rs#L126-L128) (`die_by_signal` → `raise`), which complete the hang chain.
- **Fix precision:** `guard` is already moved into `spawn_blocking` at [attach.rs:174](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/attach.rs#L174), so the second signal branch at lines 179–182 cannot call `guard.leave_bounded(...)`; it specifically needs to expose and call `terminal::discard_unread_output(SIGNAL_RESTORE_BUDGET)` after `disable_raw_mode()` (which flushes the output queue via `TCOFLUSH` to unblock both `tcdrain()` on the helper thread and Darwin process exit).
- **Severity note:** `P0` is defensible because an unkillable macOS exit hang is severe and directly violates commit `68b1f13`’s goal, though it requires a stalled terminal + daemon disconnect + SIGTERM after teardown starts (borderline P0/P1).

#### 5. Finding #5 — Unnoted design/invariant tension and follow-on effect
- Codex does not mention that [b2-design.md:13](file:///tmp/b2-design.md#L13) explicitly hedged *"Put a focused hit above the hint row where the geometry permits"* and [copy_mode.rs:964](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L964) still has the stale comment `// Cursor block, after the hint so it shows on the hint's row too`—which explains the discrepancy with commit `9567497`’s stricter invariant.
- It also omits a clean secondary symptom: once `reveal` puts `cursor` on the hint row, any subsequent `h`/`l`/`j`/`k` immediately snaps the cursor upward via `keep_cursor_in_view()`.

#### 6. Finding #7 — Blast radius understated
- Codex illustrates the bug with a single `5×5` in `2×1` example, which makes it look like a quirky edge case. In fact, for **any** image fitted to `C` cells whose source width `e` is coprime to `C` (`gcd(C, e) == 1`), panning by *any* nonzero number of cells leaves **zero** source pixels aligned to a cell edge (`lead(j) % (cell * e) == 0` requires `e | j`, impossible for `0 < j < e`), so the **entire visible image vanishes** whenever `cell_px` is `None`.

#### 7. Finding #8 — Minor precision caveat
- Codex says *"The wheel regression test never exercises a stamped wheel event"*, which is accurate for [a_wheel_opens_on_the_lines_its_frame_showed](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L9861-L9900), though the immediately following test [a_wheel_with_an_expired_stamp_says_why_it_did_nothing](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L9905-L9937) *does* pass `Some(1)` for the expired-stamp error path (and [a_wheel_tick_before_a_new_layout_is_drawn_reaches_the_pane_shown](file:///tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs#L10962-L10986) passes a frame stamp for app-forwarding). What is specifically untested is a **valid, non-latest frame stamp opening wheel copy mode** (two frames + `Some(first_frame)` + OSC 52 check).

synthesis.content:
**FIX before merging `a330fbb` into `6bc9d94`.** The reviews agree on several paths that can copy the wrong text, drop input, or render images differently in Kitty and raster. The macOS teardown path has a source-confirmed cleanup gap. Its reported exit hang still needs a targeted reproduction before assigning P0. This synthesis is based on the supplied source reviews and image-placement arithmetic. No builds or runtime tests were run.

### macOS teardown · potential P0

- **SIGTERM during terminal restoration skips output discard.** If a signal arrives after `guard.leave()` starts, the second signal branch restores terminal mode and returns without discarding pending output. Darwin may then wait for the unread PTY output during process exit. Use bounded output cleanup in both signal paths, with a fallback to the actual stdout PTY when `/dev/tty` cannot be opened. Reproduce by confirming the client has entered restoration before sending SIGTERM. A client already blocked writing a render cannot advance to restoration solely because the daemon disconnects. [Signal branch](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/attach.rs:174) · [Output cleanup](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/terminal.rs:173)

### P1 · Copy mode and input routing

1. **A stamped entry can open on the wrong terminal screen.** `Drawn` carries coordinates from the presented frame, while `CopyView::new` takes screen identity from the live VT. A primary-to-alternate switch can substitute different text or open a blank view beyond the alternate buffer. Stamp a screen generation so a primary → alternate → primary sequence also invalidates the old stamp. Distinguish screen changes from resize invalidation at `copy_mode_over` so keyboard and wheel entry cannot silently fall back to the new screen. [Copy view](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:55) · [Live fallback](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:2954)
2. **A stale stamped drag can yank from a newer page.** After a page change or horizontal pan, the drag maps through the old frame and then clamps into the current view. Cancel the gesture when the rebased stamped view differs from the current view, and clear gesture state on release. Any implementation that preserves the gesture must also extract against the stamped view. [Mouse handler](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:3083) · [Selection extraction](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:680)
3. **Copy-mode invalidation can swallow keys, paste, clicks, and wheel input.** A key is marked consumed when the renderer clears copy mode before the input handler reacquires the lock. Paste and mouse have related early-exit paths. Consume input only after resolving a valid mode, keep routing consistent across paste chunks, and resolve stale mode before app mouse and ordinary selection dispatch. [Input routing](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:1352) · [Mouse dispatch](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:1617)
4. **Horizontal search pans truncate keyboard selections.** The anchor survives a pan, but extraction clips to the new viewport and drops selected text. Define source-coordinate extraction for panned selections, including intermediate rows and wide glyphs. Assert the clipboard bytes in both pan directions. [Selection extraction](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:680) · [Existing test](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:1427)
5. **Scrollback eviction can silently shorten an upward selection.** If the cursor’s row is evicted while the anchor survives, rebasing substitutes the oldest surviving row. Apply eviction checks to both endpoints and assert `SelectionEvicted` with no clipboard write. [Rebase](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:255)
6. **Search can place the cursor under the hint bar.** A match on the final source row can paint its first glyph over the hint and let `y` copy that glyph. Use the readable height for navigation so the final row can scroll into view, and keep the cursor inside the readable area. [Viewport bounds](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:127) · [Search positioning](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:594)

### P1 · Kitty and raster parity

- **Host image ID reuse can reverse stacking relative to raster.** Re-placing an image can move it to the end of raster’s paint order while Kitty keeps its earlier position under equal-`z` ID ordering. This affects both same-ID and new-ID placement reuse. Encode shux placement order in Kitty `z`, keep it within `[-2^30, -1]` for overlay layering, and avoid unnecessary updates to surviving placements. [Kitty emitter](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs:175) · [Raster paint order](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-raster/src/lib.rs:490)
- **Cropped images can disappear or lose most visible rows without cell-pixel metrics.** Older clients and terminals that omit pixel dimensions take a fallback that searches for an exactly aligned source pixel. Cover both disappearance and excessive truncation, horizontally and vertically. Falling back only when no aligned pixel exists leaves the truncation case broken. [Placement math](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/kitty_emit.rs:294)

### P2 and evidence gaps

- **The wheel regression test misses the valid older-stamp path.** Publish two frames with different text, send a wheel event stamped with the first, and assert the literal OSC 52 payload from that frame. Existing stamped tests cover expiry and app forwarding. [Wheel test](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:9861)
- **The exit frame can retain the `Y` copy-mode indicator.** Build the indicator from the resolved mode used for that frame. [Frame construction](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/attach.rs:2221) · [Status text](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux/src/statusbar_build.rs:184)
- **Short-row newline loss and SGR bleed remain unverified.** Both mechanisms follow from the code if a presented row has missing cells, but the proposed mixed-width fixture has no demonstrated production path. Establish a reachable fixture before treating these as release blockers. [Grid resize](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:1526) · [Copy rendering](/private/tmp/b2-council/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:793)
